source_text:
Fragmentum in epistulam ad Philemonem (in catenis)
Phm
1,1 Ἐν πολλαῖς ἐπιστολαῖς ξένον τίθησι ῥῆμα τοῦ μέλλοντος εἰσάγεσθαι λόγου
κατασκευαστικόν, καὶ νῦν ἐπειδὴ ἔμελλεν ἀξιοῦν ὑπὲρ Ὀνησίμου τῇ ἑαυτοῦ ἀξίᾳ–
ἀξία δὲ αὐτοῦ τὸ δεδέσθαι–, τὸ ἀξιόπιστον τῆς παρακλήσεως δείκνυσιν.
thought_title: Paul's unusual word prepares his appeal
orientation: Oecumenius begins his comment on Philemon 1:1 by explaining a general habit of Paul's letters, then applies it to the present case of Onesimus.
pass_a_gloss: In many letters he places an unusual word that prepares the argument about to be introduced, and now since he was about to make an appeal on behalf of Onesimus by his own worth—and his worth is his imprisonment—he shows the credibility of the appeal.

lemmas.gloss: to make a request, to ask

choices.why: Keeps the literal sense of ξένος as unusual or foreign, matching the source's emphasis on a distinctive term Paul inserts.
Renders the adjective as a relative clause to keep the literal force of 'constructive/preparatory' while fitting English word order.
The glossary bans 'request' for παρακλήσεως but not for ἀξιοῦν; this rendering keeps the verb's sense of asking on the basis of worth.
Uses the glossary's required English 'worth' for ἀξίᾳ and keeps the dative of means literal.
Uses the glossary's required English 'imprisonment' for δεδέσθαι, treating the perfect infinitive as a substantive.
Uses the glossary's required English for both ἀξιόπιστον and παρακλήσεως.

bible_refs.note: The fragment comments on this verse, where Paul mentions his imprisonment as he writes about Onesimus.

pass_b_english: In many letters Paul places an unusual word that prepares for the argument he is about to introduce. Here too, since he was about to make an appeal on behalf of Onesimus, he shows the credibility of the appeal by his own worth—and his worth is his imprisonment.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'appeal' for παρακλήσεως, but 'strange' for ξένον is not banned; however, 'word' is flat. More critically, 'strange' misses the technical sense of 'unusual/foreign' as preparatory device.
last_rejected.fix: In many letters Paul places an unusual word that prepares for the argument he is about to introduce.
last_rejected.ruling: ξένον means 'strange/unusual/foreign'; rendering as 'strange' is within normal range, not a major error.

problems.why: Same Greek term rendered two ways; reader may think different concepts.
problems.fix: Standardize to 'unusual word' or 'strange word' throughout.

problems.why: Same action described with different verbs; 'request' vs 'appeal'.
Definite article vs possessive changes emphasis; reader may miss Paul's ownership.
Same Greek term rendered two ways across parallel sections; reader may think different words are meant.
problems.fix: Standardize to one English rendering across all sections.

problems.why: 'Request' and 'appeal' alternate for the same concept; reader may miss they are identical.
problems.fix: Use one term consistently across all parallel sections.

problems.why: Definite article vs. possessive pronoun before 'imprisonment' across parallel sections.
problems.fix: Standardize to one phrasing across all sections.

fixed: Standardized 'strange word' to 'unusual word' in English and gloss.
Standardized 'make a request' to 'make an appeal' in English and gloss.
Standardized 'the imprisonment' to 'his imprisonment' in English and gloss.
